content.text: {"grade": 1, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The central Lemma (pairwise-intersecting family of finite sets has finitely many minimal finite transversals) is false, and its inductive proof is invalid; the crux of the problem is thus unproved.", "errors": [{"description": "The Lemma is false. Take C={c1,c2} and F={C}\u222a{{c2}\u222ag : g\u2208G}, which is pairwise intersecting for any family G of finite sets. Its finite transversals avoiding c2 are {c1}\u222a(transversal of G), and a family G of finite sets can have infinitely many pairwise-incomparable minimal finite transversals, so no finite list B_1,...,B_s exists.", "quote": "If every two members of $\\mathcal F$ intersect, then there are finitely many nonempty finite sets $B_1,\\ldots,B_s\\subseteq P$ such that, for every finite $X\\subseteq P$,"}, {"description": "The induction is also internally broken: the hypothesis only characterizes transversals meeting C, yet is applied to F_c for a transversal X that need not meet C\\{c}. Example F={{1,2},{2,3},{2,4}}, C={1,2}: the construction yields the list {{2},{1,2}}, missing the transversal {1,3,4}, which meets C but contains no listed set.", "quote": "Conversely, a transversal $X$ meeting $C$ contains some $c\\in C$ and traverses $\\mathcal F_c$, so it contains a corresponding $D_{c,k}$."}, {"description": "The paragraph justifying the inductive criterion is incoherent (it asserts C is a member of F 'whenever this assertion is applied below', then retracts to transversals meeting C), papering over the gap rather than proving anything.", "quote": "Every transversal $X$ of $\\mathcal F$ meets $C$, since $C$ itself is a member of $\\mathcal F$ whenever this assertion is applied below; more generally, for the inductive assertion we only need to restrict attention to transversals meeting $C$."}], "notes": "Correct, easy parts: F={P(a_i)} is pairwise intersecting, and the sequence is the increasing enumeration of S={x: gcd(x,a_i)>1 for all i}; periodicity of S would finish. All genuine difficulty is deferred to a false lemma."}
